title: Tanzanian Coconut Prawns
community: Zanzibar restaurant scene — the coastal luxury starter
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Kamba wa Nazi — large prawns sautéed in foaming coconut oil and butter with garlic, cardamom, and fresh coriander. The simplest and most elegant Zanzibar prawn preparation — when the prawns are this fresh, nothing more is needed.
longDesc: Kamba wa Nazi is simplicity elevated — large fresh prawns, coconut oil, garlic, and the lightest Zanzibar spice touch. This is the restaurant starter that makes visitors understand why Zanzibar seafood is world-class.
ingredients: 500g large prawns — peeled, deveined, tails on
steps: Heat coconut oil and butter over very high heat until foaming.
Add prawns in a single layer. Cook without touching 90 seconds.
Add garlic, cardamom, and chilli. Flip prawns.
Cook 60—90 seconds on the other side.
Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve immediately.
cookingScience: Coconut oil has a higher smoke point than olive oil — it achieves the rapid high-temperature sear needed for prawns without burning.
sustainabilityTips: Morning-fresh Indian Ocean prawns from local Zanzibari fishermen.
culturalNote: Kamba wa Nazi is Zanzibar hospitality at its purest — the best ingredient, the simplest treatment, the greatest result.
